items.q: On Capitol Hill, Jolly was considered a centrist among House Republicans. He was ranked the 48th most bipartisan lawmaker by the Lugar Center in 2016, and supported a balanced budget amendment and a ban on offshore drilling.

items.t: Proposed passing a Florida statute that replicates the Roe v. Wade and Casey v. Planned Parenthood framework, making abortion legal until fetal viability (2025).
items.q: Through statutory codification. He proposes passing a Florida statute that replicates the Roe v. Wade and Casey v. Planned Parenthood framework: abortion legal until fetal viability (approximately 23 to 24 weeks)

items.t: Supports more stringent background checks covering all forms of changing gun ownership, including gifting within families, and supports banning assault weapons.
items.q: He favors much more stringent background checks, covering all forms of changing gun ownership including gifting within families, and banning assault weapons.

items.t: Supports licensing, registration, and insurance of firearms.
items.q: I’m now for the licensing, registration, and insurance of firearms.

items.t: Introduced legislation in June 2015 to expand the ban on drilling in the Eastern Gulf (2015).
items.q: In June 2015, Jolly introduced legislation to expand the ban on drilling in the Eastern Gulf.

items.t: Supports giving qualified in-state students preferred application status at Florida's public universities (2026).
items.q: David Jolly believes qualified Florida students who work hard in Florida high schools should have preferred application status at Florida's public universities.

items.t: Introduced the bipartisan Stop Act, together with Rep. Rick Nolan, to prevent members of Congress from personally soliciting campaign contributions.
items.q: Republican David Jolly (Fla.) and Democrat Rick Nolan (Minn.) targeted Congress itself when they introduced the Stop Act: it would to prevent members of Congress from personally soliciting campaign contributions.
